title: Mount Rushmore's last day
photoNote: Mount Rushmore in July 1939, with scaffolding between Jefferson and Lincoln over the unfinished head of Theodore Roosevelt. Public Roads Administration photo 30-N-40-2431 (NARA 135804230), unrestricted, public domain. Two years before work ended.
body:
For fourteen years, nearly 400 workers rode down a granite cliff on steel cables to carve it with dynamite. Not one of them died.

31 October 1941. Work on Mount Rushmore came to an end. Gutzon Borglum, the sculptor who designed it, had died that March, and his son Lincoln Borglum carried the job to its finish.

About 90 percent of the carving was done with dynamite, blasting until only inches of rock were left. Workers climbed 700 stairs to the top each morning, then were lowered over the face in bosun chairs. One remembered the pay as $8 a day.

Five weeks later came Pearl Harbor.

Would you have ridden down that mountain in a bosun chair?

#OnThisDay #WW2
